=== AC5: THE BLINDNESS GUARD, MUTATION-VERIFIED. It can actually fail, for the right reason. ===
tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_transport_param_typing_cc77.py — an AST check over every core
reconciler module (adapters/ excluded: they IMPLEMENT the port rather than consume it).

A test that has never been seen red is not evidence. Each of the three bad spellings was applied to
a REAL parameter (dispatch_one.create_one's client) and the suite re-run:

  MUTATION 1  client            (bare)            -> 1 failed, 56 passed
  MUTATION 2  client: Any                         -> 1 failed, 56 passed
  MUTATION 3  from rebar_reconciler._backend import TicketTransport  (shim path)
                                                  -> 1 failed, 56 passed
  RESTORED                                        -> 57 passed

Every failure is 'AssertionError: port-typing violations:' raised at the test's own assert, in the
parametrised case [dispatch_one.py] — i.e. the check FIRED. Not an AttributeError, not an
ImportError, not a collection error. Mutation 3 matters most: it is the only one where the source
still reads 'client: TicketTransport' and mypy still passes clean, so nothing else in the repo
would have caught it.

The exemption set is a single pinned entry, asserted by a second test so it cannot quietly grow into
an allowlist; that test also re-derives the exempt function from the AST, so a stale exemption fails
rather than silently covering nothing.

=== AC6: NOTHING WAS WEAKENED ===
git diff origin/main..HEAD touches _backend.py only by APPENDING a comment block. _TransportPortMeta,
assert_transport_conforms(), the required-member list, and the AST audit are byte-unchanged (no diff
hunk intersects them). Reconciler unit suite: 1821 passed, 1 xfailed, UNEDITED — no test needed
changing, which is the change's own premise (annotations + import form only, zero behaviour).

=== MODULE SIZES (800 hard cap) — one real constraint hit, and how it was resolved ===
dispatch_one.py sat at 796/800 BEFORE this change, so its six annotations (+7 lines, mostly one
signature ruff must explode past 100 cols) did NOT fit. Resolved by moving the two PURE link-probe
helpers (_index_existing_links / _find_link_id) to dispatch_apply_phases.py — the leaf that already
holds update_one's other extracted phases — and re-importing them, so dispatch_one.<name> attribute
access and bare-name calls resolve unchanged. They depend on nothing in dispatch_one.

  dispatch_one.py           796 -> 759
  dispatch_apply_phases.py  170 -> 226
  _backend.py               599 -> 622
  applier.py                795 -> 800 (at the cap, under it; gate is strictly '>')
  outbound_differ.py        792 -> 799
  all others                well under

A FIRST attempt also moved _call_with_retry into a new leaf. It is NOT behaviour-neutral and was
ABANDONED: 6 tests monkeypatch dispatch_one.time / dispatch_one.RetryExhaustedError, which
_call_with_retry reads as module globals, so relocating it silently changes what those patches
affect. Recording the rejected route so nobody re-attempts it: _call_with_retry stays in dispatch_one.

Also measured and rejected: a RUNTIME relative import ('from ._backend import ...'). It breaks 10
tests with 'attempted relative import with no known parent package' — several test modules load
reconciler modules by file path, with no parent package. The port import must be TYPE_CHECKING-
guarded, and capability narrowing must use a STRING cast target so no runtime import is needed.
Both facts are non-obvious and cost a full suite run each to find.
